headline: GOLD CLOSES WEEK AT $4,477, SILVER NEAR $67 — CPI SEPTEMBER 11 IS THE FULCRUM AS FOMC RATE-HIKE BETS SETTLE AT 50/50
snippet: Gold settled near $4,477/oz to close the week — recovering from Wednesday's NFP-driven low of $4,374 after Fed Governor Waller's dovish remarks trimmed September rate-hike odds from 70% to approximately 50%. Silver ended near $67. With US markets closed Saturday, investors turn to the most consequential macro calendar of the year: ADP employment Wednesday, PPI Thursday, and August CPI on September 11, just five days before the Federal Reserve's September 15–16 FOMC meeting. Gold's holding range into that data is $4,313–$4,645; a soft CPI sets up a run at $4,700+ while a hot print risks retesting September lows.

headline: VIZSLA COPPER HITS 49.2m @ 4.7% CuEq AT PALMER ALASKA — ZONE 1 HIGH-GRADE VMS CORE EXTENDS DOWNDIP; TSXV: VCU
snippet: Vizsla Copper (TSXV: VCU / OTCQX: VCUFF) released initial assay results from its 12,250-metre diamond drill program at the Palmer Copper-Zinc VMS Project in Southeast Alaska. Hole CMR26-199 returned 49.2 metres grading 4.7% CuEq — including a 27.0-metre high-grade core at 8.4% CuEq (5.46% Cu, 8.55% Zn, 39.12 g/t Ag). A second hole 50 metres downdip confirmed Zone 1 continuity at 40.4 metres @ 3.0% CuEq. Palmer is a world-class VMS system in one of the most copper-prolific geological corridors in North America; these are the best 2026 results to date and point to a larger deposit than the existing inferred resource.

headline: KENORLAND HITS 204 g/t GOLD AT WESTERN WABIGOON IN MAIDEN DRILL — 8 OF 9 HOLES MINERALIZED; TSXV: KLD
snippet: Kenorland Minerals (TSXV: KLD) reported maiden diamond drill results from the Western Wabigoon Project in northwestern Ontario, held under option with Centerra Gold. Gold mineralisation was confirmed in eight of nine holes across a 4,089-metre program testing 1.9 kilometres of the W2 target. Standout intercept: hole 26DFDD003 returned 1.05 metres at 204.34 g/t gold, including 0.50 metres at 428.5 g/t, inside a broader zone returning 37.75 metres at 0.30 g/t. The shear-hosted, hydrothermal system in a classic Ontario greenstone belt setting — optioned by Centerra — warrants follow-up drilling.

headline: AZTEC MINERALS EXTENDS TOMBSTONE 255m TO 1,250m OF OXIDE STRIKE — BEST HOLE 83.8m @ 1.31 g/t AuEq; TSXV: AZT
snippet: Aztec Minerals Corp. (TSXV: AZT / OTCQB: AZZTF) extended the Contention oxide gold-silver system at its Tombstone Property in southeastern Arizona by 255 metres to over 1,250 metres of continuously drilled strike length. All five North Extension holes hit mineralisation. Best result: hole TR26-41 returned 83.8 metres at 1.31 g/t AuEq (0.90 g/t Au, 22.61 g/t Ag), including 7.6 metres at 8.34 g/t AuEq. Nine additional holes (TR26-45 to TR26-53) are drilled and awaiting assay; the zone remains open along strike and at depth.

headline: GREENLAND MINES CLOSES SARFARTOQ DEAL — ONE DEPOSIT WOULD SUPPLY 34% OF GLOBAL NdPr OUTSIDE CHINA; $2.05B NPV; NASDAQ: GRML
snippet: Greenland Mines Ltd. (NASDAQ: GRML) completed the acquisition of the Sarfartoq Nd-Pr Rare Earths Project in southwest Greenland on September 1, 2026, following Government of Greenland approval. The deal — $20 million cash plus $15 million in securities for Neo North Star Resources — brings a project whose ST1 deposit alone, at 2025 consumption levels, would represent approximately 34% of all NdPr oxide refined outside China annually across nine scheduled production years. The project carries a pre-tax NPV of approximately $2.05 billion and an IRR of 118.6%. Infill drilling, pilot metallurgical work, and a pre-feasibility study begin immediately. Neo Performance Materials retains offtake rights to up to 60% of future output.

headline: URANIUM SLIDES TO $79.60/LB NEAR 3-YEAR LOW — KAZATOMPROM CUTS 2026 GUIDANCE 10% AS H1 OUTPUT PARADOXICALLY RISES
snippet: Uranium spot prices fell to approximately $79.60/lb as of September 3 — near their lowest level since November 2023 — even as Kazatomprom announced a roughly 10% cut to its 2026 production guidance (to 27,500–29,000 tU). The paradox: Kazatomprom's first-half 2026 output was actually higher year-on-year, negating near-term supply fears. Cameco separately flagged logistical disruption at McArthur River from May flooding but says both it and Kazatomprom remain on track to meet full-year targets. The $79.60 spot price challenges the dominant bullish uranium narrative from earlier in 2026 and raises the question of whether demand has been sufficiently front-loaded.

headline: CPM GROUP STANDS ASIDE IN GOLD — $4,320-$4,670 TARGET THROUGH SEPTEMBER 16; CPI DATA WILL SET THE DIRECTION
snippet: CPM Group's September 4 trade signal advises gold traders to stand aside rather than initiate new positions, citing extreme expected volatility around the August CPI (September 11) and FOMC decision (September 16). CPM identifies $4,320–$4,670 as the anticipated trading envelope through the meeting, with the CPI print as the decisive variable. A CPI at or below 3.0% year-on-year could trigger a significant breakout above $4,645; a hot print opens a retest of $4,313. CPM says the risk-reward is unfavourable for speculation ahead of binary data — standing aside is itself a position.

headline: GOLD BULLS TARGET $5,051 BY MONTH-END — ANALYSTS SPLIT BETWEEN $5,304 UPSIDE AND $4,136 FLOOR FOR SEPTEMBER
snippet: Gold's base-case September price target of $5,051/oz — per composite analyst surveys — requires the August CPI to confirm disinflation and the Fed to signal a hold at the September 16 meeting, a scenario with better-than-even odds now that rate-hike bets have retreated to 50%. The wide $4,136–$5,304 range for September reflects a binary macro setup: a hot print sends gold testing 2026 lows while a softer read sets up the strongest September for gold since 2010. Analysts flagged PPI on September 10 as the first signal — PPI is often a leading indicator for the CPI print that follows.

headline: COPPER MARKET STAYS STRUCTURALLY SPLIT — COMEX NEAR RECORD INVENTORY WHILE LME DRAINS; $6.56/LB HOLDING
snippet: Copper closed the week near $6.56/lb — recovering from Friday's NFP-driven dip to $6.40 — as the structural bifurcation between U.S. and non-U.S. markets continued to widen. Comex warehouses remain near record highs from tariff-driven front-loading, while LME stocks outside the U.S. keep drawing down on genuine Chinese and Southeast Asian consumption. Chile's ongoing output shortfall (-9.4% year-on-year in July) and Congo export disruptions make the non-tariff supply picture fundamentally tight. Analysts say the Comex overhang is a tariff artifact, not a global supply signal — the real copper market is still tight.

headline: RARE EARTHS COULD BE MINING'S NEXT BILLION-DOLLAR OPPORTUNITY — DEFENSE AND OEM DEMAND OUTPACING WESTERN SUPPLY BUILDOUT
snippet: As China's rare earth export suspension approaches its November 10, 2026 expiration, OEM manufacturers and defence contractors are accelerating Western supply chain development — creating what analysts call the sector's next major investment opportunity. Four structural demand drivers are converging: permanent magnets for EV motors, wind turbines, defence systems, and robotics. With MP Materials now shipping NdFeB magnets from Fort Worth under a 10-year Pentagon contract and Greenland Mines closing the Sarfartoq acquisition, the mine-to-magnet supply chain race is transitioning from policy priority to commercial execution. The 65-day countdown to the November 10 suspension expiry is the sector's sharpest near-term catalyst.

headline: GOLD IS BREAKING OUT — CAN SOFTER CPI SUSTAIN THE RALLY? Technical Analysis Points To $4,700 If Data Cooperates
snippet: StockCharts technical analysis finds gold in a potential breakout structure after recovering from the NFP-driven low of $4,374 to $4,477 — a move that re-established bullish momentum above the 20-day moving average. Key resistance is at $4,645; the next measured move targets $4,700+ if August CPI on September 11 confirms disinflation. A close above $4,500 this coming week would be the confirming signal technical traders are watching for. A CPI miss flips the setup to neutral with $4,313 as the first support and $4,136 as the floor. The analysis notes that gold's recovery from the NFP selloff was faster than bearish consensus expected.
